report.summary: Analyzed chunk 4 of 9 of daedalus/mapping/inventory.py: functions _clean_annotation, annotation_overreach, _module_targets, harvest with docstring claims.
risks: annotation_overreach | medium | Docstring claims 'annotation keys carrying fields a human is NOT allowed to set' but function checks keys in annotations Mapping where values are Mappings, and reports extra keys. This is consistent but note that non-Mapping values are also reported as bad. | Verify if non-Mapping values should be considered overreach.

harvest | medium | Docstring claims 'Returns (annotations, narrative_features, stats)' but code returns (annotations, narrative, stats) where narrative is a list, not a dict. | Check if the return type matches the docstring claim.

harvest | low | Docstring claims 'LOSSLESS by contract' and 'Nothing is dropped'. However, the code filters features with _clean_annotation and only includes fields that are non-empty strings. Some fields might be silently dropped if they are not strings or have no content. | Verify lossless behavior with non-string or empty fields.

harvest | medium | Docstring claims 'Already-schema-2 documents pass their blocks straight through'. The code checks if old.get('schema') == SCHEMA, but SCHEMA is not defined in this chunk. | Ensure SCHEMA is defined elsewhere and is correctly set for schema-2.
todos: Verify that SCHEMA constant is defined and represents schema-2.
Confirm that the return type of harvest matches the docstring (narrative vs narrative_features).
Check if _clean_annotation and harvest correctly handle all human fields without dropping data.

handoff.purpose: Define functions for cleaning annotations, detecting human-unallowed fields, resolving module targets, and harvesting human data from old inventory.

symbols.name: _clean_annotation
symbols.note: Private function that filters a raw annotation dict to only include allowed keys with non-empty string values.

symbols.name: annotation_overreach
symbols.note: Public function returning list of annotation keys that contain fields not allowed for human setting.

symbols.name: _module_targets
symbols.note: Private function returning list of known modules that a feature's entrypoints resolve to.

symbols.name: harvest
symbols.note: Public function that lifts human half from old inventory into annotations and narrative features.

claims.text: Annotation keys carrying fields a human is NOT allowed to set.
claims.why: The function iterates over annotation items and checks for keys not in the allowed set (FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS, AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS). It returns a list of such keys.

claims.text: Reported rather than silently dropped. Silently dropping is how a person concludes the field works; naming it is how they learn the rule.
claims.why: The function returns a list of bad keys, thus reporting them instead of dropping.

claims.text: The build ignores these fields either way -- an annotation that could set ``status`` would hand the hand-written file's exact power back through a side door.
claims.why: The claim about build behavior is outside the scope of this chunk.

claims.text: Every module a hand-written feature's entrypoints resolve to. ALL of them, not the first: the kairos-rename shim entry names five modules in one feature, and attaching its rationale to only one of them would lose the reason for the other four.
claims.why: The function iterates over all entrypoints and collects all matching known modules, not just the first.

claims.text: Lift the human half out of a previous inventory. LOSSLESS by contract.
claims.why: The claim of losslessness cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone; it depends on external behavior and the handling of all fields.
The code returns (annotations, narrative, stats) where narrative is a list, not a dict. The docstring says 'narrative_features' but the variable is named 'narrative'.

claims.text: Every feature in the old document ends up in exactly one of the two: an annotation keyed to the module(s) its entrypoints name, or a verbatim narrative feature.
claims.why: The code processes features: if targets exist, it adds to annotations; if no targets, it adds to narrative. Each feature goes to exactly one.

claims.text: Nothing is dropped, because a generated file that discards the rationale somebody wrote is not progress -- it is the same rot with a fresher timestamp.
claims.why: The claim about nothing being dropped cannot be fully verified from this chunk; it depends on the handling of all data fields.

claims.text: Already-schema-2 documents pass their blocks straight through; the harvest only has work to do the first time.
claims.why: The code checks if old.get('schema') == SCHEMA, but SCHEMA is not defined in this chunk. The behavior depends on the value of SCHEMA.

observations.what: Function annotation_overreach uses allowed set from FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS, AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS but these are not defined in this chunk.
Function _module_targets uses _TOKEN_RE which is not defined in this chunk.
Function harvest uses SCHEMA constant not defined in this chunk.
Docstring says returns 'narrative_features' but code returns variable 'narrative'.

In harvest, for schema-2 documents, annotations are cleaned with _clean_annotation using FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS + ENV_HUMAN_FIELDS + AREA_HUMAN_FIELDS, but for old-style features, only FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS are extracted. This discrepancy may drop env/area human fields from old-style features.

In harvest, for old-style features, human fields are extracted only from FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS, but _clean_annotation is not used. The docstring claims losslessness, but this may drop non-string or empty fields.
